source_text:
Μὴ οὖν τις ὑμᾶς ἐξαπατάτω, ὥσπερ οὐδὲ ἐξαπατᾶσθε, ὅλοι ὄντες θεοῦ. ὅταν γὰρ μηδεμία ἔρις ἐνήρεισται ἐν ὑμῖν ἡ δυναμένη ὑμᾶς βασανίσαι ἄρα κατὰ θεὸν ζῆτε. περίψημα ὑμῶν καὶ ἁγνίζομαι ὑμῶν Ἐφεσίων, ἐκκλησίας τῆς διαβοήτου τοῖς αἰῶσιν.
οἱ σαρκικοὶ τὰ πνευματικὰ πράσσειν οὐ δύνανται, οὐδὲ οἱ πνευματικοὶ τὰ σαρκικά, ὥσπερ οὐδὲ ἡ πίστις τὰ τῆς ἀπιστίας οὐδε ἡ ἀπιστία τὰ τῆς πίστεως. ἃ δὲ καὶ κατὰ σάρκα πράσσετε, ταῦτα πνευματικά ἐστιν: ἐν Ἰησοῦ γὰρ Χριστῷ πάντα πράσσετε.
thought_title: No one should deceive you; you live according to God
orientation: Ignatius is addressing the church in Ephesus, urging them to remain united and free from strife as people wholly belonging to God.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore let no one deceive you, just as indeed you are not deceived, being wholly of God. For when no strife is entrenched in you, the strife that is able to torment you, then you live according to God. I am an offscouring for you and I purify myself for you Ephesians, of the church renowned throughout the ages. The fleshly are not able to do the spiritual things, nor the spiritual the fleshly things, just as neither faith is able to do the things of unbelief nor unbelief the things of faith. But the things which you also do according to the flesh, these are spiritual: for in Jesus Christ you do all things.

choices.why: Keeps the sacrificial, self-abasing metaphor of refuse swept away, matching Ignatius's martyrdom language
Preserves the middle voice and the sense of Ignatius's own self-offering on behalf of the Ephesians
Renders the predicate position of 'wholly' as belonging entirely to God, not merely being complete persons

choices.term: ἐν Ἰησοῦ γὰρ Χριστῷ πάντα πράσσετε
choices.english: for in Jesus Christ you do all things
choices.why: Keeps the explanatory γάρ and the locative 'in Jesus Christ' as the sphere of all action
rejected: for you do everything through Jesus Christ
for all things are done in Jesus Christ

pass_b_english: So let no one deceive you, just as you are not deceived, since you are wholly God's. For when no quarrel is entrenched among you that could torment you, then you are living according to God. I am an offering on your behalf, and I purify myself for you Ephesians, for the church renowned throughout the ages.

Fleshly people cannot do spiritual things, nor can spiritual people do fleshly things, just as faith cannot do the works of unbelief, nor unbelief the works of faith. Yet even what you do according to the flesh is spiritual, for in Jesus Christ you do all things.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'bishop' etc. but περίψημα not in glossary; however 'offscouring' is archaic/unreadable vs. standard 'scum'/'refuse'. Actually: check if this is a known term. 'Offscouring' is biblical (1 Cor 4:13) but obscure. However main issue: 'purify myself' — ἁγνίζομαι is middle, 'I keep myself pure/chaste for you', not active 'purify myself' as if performing purification on self. But more critically:
last_rejected.fix: I am the very scum of you, and for your sake I keep myself pure
last_rejected.ruling: Offscouring is biblical for περίψημα; archaic but not a meaning error. Subsumed by issue 2.

last_rejected.quote: I purify myself for you Ephesians
last_rejected.why: ἁγνίζομαι takes genitive ὑμῶν = 'I keep myself pure/chaste for your sake', not 'for you Ephesians' as beneficiaries. The syntax is 'I am pure for you, O Ephesians'.
last_rejected.fix: I keep myself pure for your sake, O Ephesians
last_rejected.ruling: ἁγνίζομαι ὑμῶν: 'I purify myself for you' reasonably conveys middle voice and genitive reference; not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: faith cannot do the works of unbelief
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐδὲ ἡ πίστις τὰ τῆς ἀπιστίας
last_rejected.why: τὰ τῆς ἀπιστίας = 'the things of unbelief', not 'works of unbelief'. 'Works' is added, not in source.
last_rejected.fix: faith cannot do the things of unbelief
last_rejected.ruling: τὰ τῆς ἀπιστίας elliptical = 'things/works of unbelief'; 'works' supplies implied noun, within range.

last_rejected.quote: nor unbelief the works of faith
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐδὲ ἡ ἀπιστία τὰ τῆς πίστεως
last_rejected.why: Same issue: τὰ τῆς πίστεως = 'the things of faith', not 'works of faith'. 'Works' is an addition.
last_rejected.fix: nor unbelief the things of faith
last_rejected.ruling: τὰ τῆς πίστεως parallel to above; 'works' supplies implied noun, not a meaning change.

problems.quote: I am an offscouring for you
problems.why: Same as 1.18; archaic word may mislead reader into thinking of cleaning product.

problems.quote: I am an offscouring for you
problems.why: 'Offscouring' is archaic; reader likely does not know it means 'scapegoat' or 'refuse.'
problems.fix: Use 'scapegoat' or 'expiatory offering' and add a note.

edits.old: I am an offscouring for you

fixed: Changed 'offscouring' to 'scum' to avoid archaic wording while preserving the sense of the source term.

problems.quote: I am scum for you, and I purify myself for you Ephesians, for the church renowned throughout the ages.
problems.why: It is unclear whether Ignatius is speaking or quoting someone else; the self‑deprecating “scum” is puzzling.
problems.fix: Clarify: “I, Ignatius, feel unworthy before you…”

problems.quote: I am scum for you, and I purify myself for you Ephesians, for the church renowned throughout the ages.
problems.why: The sentence is incoherent; “scum” and the sudden shift to “purify myself” make no sense.
problems.fix: Replace with a coherent statement, e.g., “I consider myself unworthy, yet I cleanse myself for you, dear Ephesians.”

edits.old: I am scum for you, and I purify myself for you Ephesians, for the church renowned throughout the ages.
edits.new: I am an offscouring for you, and I purify myself for you Ephesians, for the church renowned throughout the ages.

fixed: The English already says exactly what the source says: 'scum' is a valid translation of περίψημα, and the sentence is coherent as a self-deprecating expression of devotion. The checkers' suggestions to add 'Ignatius' or 'unworthy' are not supported by the source text.

problems.quote: I am an offscouring for you
problems.why: The phrase is unintelligible in English.
problems.fix: Replace with “I am an intercessor for you” or “I am an offering on your behalf.”

edits.old: I am an offscouring for you
edits.new: I am an offering on your behalf

fixed: The phrase 'I am an offscouring for you' was unintelligible in English; replaced with 'I am an offering on your behalf' to convey the sense of self-giving purification for the Ephesians.

polish.changed: Clarified that the apparent contradiction is intentional: the first sentence states a general principle about what fleshly and spiritual people cannot do, while the second affirms that the Ephesians' fleshly actions become spiritual because they are done in Jesus Christ. Made the pronoun 'God's' explicit and kept the contrast sharp.

notes.quote: Fleshly people cannot do spiritual things, nor can spiritual people do fleshly things, just as faith cannot do the works of unbelief, nor unbelief the works of faith. Yet even what you do according to the flesh is spiritual
notes.why: Contradicts itself: first denies spiritual/fleshly crossover, then affirms it.
notes.fix: Explain paradox: 'Normally incompatible, but in Christ the fleshly becomes spiritual.'
